statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 20% holds the lower edge of the watch band while Stress stays high at 78%.
recommendation: Tail remains at the watch floor because the overnight NQ path is two-sided inside an unchanged band and the session high has not been retaken, so the mapped state is WATCH rather than a block. Stress stays high on long-end Treasury yields near 24-year highs, a conflict-premium energy complex and the September payrolls release at 12:30Z. The flagged window is narrow, spanning 12:30Z to 15:00Z around the release and the U.S. cash open.
headline: NQ holds an unchanged overnight band as Asia diverges into the September payrolls checkpoint
body: NQ futures trade 30,896.25 (+0.44%) inside an unchanged overnight range of 30,760.25-30,920.00, in the upper half of the band but without retaking the 30,920.00 high. Cash NDX closed 30,501.56 (+0.31%) on October 1 with a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range, and VIX finished at 16.39. The macro backdrop remains far more stressed than the price path: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.342% on Thursday, its highest since early 2002 and the biggest quarterly rise this century in Q3, before easing to about 5.25%, while the 2-year sits near 4.80%. Brent at 102.10 and WTI at 92.49 retain a conflict premium after Thursday's move above 102, though both eased slightly overnight. Asia is weaker and thin: the Nikkei 225 trades 68,304.33 (-0.95%), mainland China is closed for Golden Week and India is closed for Gandhi Jayanti, so a firmer NQ represents cross-asset divergence rather than aligned momentum. Tokyo core CPI printed 2.7% against a 2.4% forecast with the core-core measure at 3.0%, the first reading above the Bank of Japan's target since January, lifting pricing for an October hike and adding a global long-end rates dimension. The dollar holds near its firmest since May 2025. The September employment report lands at 12:30Z with consensus near 85k-95k against August's 162k, unemployment seen at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.3%. Absent observed persistent one-way structure, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension, event importance and elevated volatility are scored into Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. The shared Finviz context file was not used this run: its latest publication is roughly 53 hours old and marked partial, well outside the 90-minute freshness contract, so the assessment rests on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band apart from one orange hour at 06:00Z on October 1, when Tail touched 25% on a brief trend-up read. Tail then settled back to 20-24% and has printed 20% for the last ten hours. Stress drifted up from 71% to a 79% peak as the long-end yield selloff intensified through Thursday before easing to 78%, and Confidence held at 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail at the watch floor through the remaining Asian and European hours while the overnight band contains price, steps it to 21-22% into the pre-release hours as liquidity thins, and reaches the 25% block threshold only conditionally for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering the U.S. cash open and the delayed-second-leg window after the payrolls print. That elevation is contingent on an aligned opening auction, shallow pullbacks and a long-end yield break back above 5.342%, not on the release itself. Stress peaks in the extreme band at 83% around the release and decays through the afternoon. From 21:00Z the weekend futures halt means no live price path forms, so the remaining slots hold the watch floor with Stress and Confidence stepping down, and the next checkpoints are the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, ISM Services on October 5 and the FOMC minutes on October 7.

Orderly two-way discovery would invalidate it.
